subject: Nimbus Health — VPC/On‑Prem Deployment acceptance criteria and next steps
body:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: it_ops@nimbushealth.com, Procurement Team <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment prerequisites — network/KMS/audit items

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Nimbus is ready to move forward with the private deployment pilot but my security and IT teams asked for a single consolidated acceptance checklist we can run against our environment. Specifically they want:
- Network requirements (subnet, NAT, firewall rules, ingress/egress ports)
- KMS/HSM key provisioning guidance and required IAM roles
- Audit/logging endpoints and retention — where do logs land and how are they queried?
- Minimum host/GPU sizing and quantization guidance for a 250 rps baseline
- A sample network diagram we can attach to our ticket

Can you send over a checklist and any templates we should fill out? Also please flag any items that usually block a go/no-go for on‑prem or VPC installs.

Appreciate it — we have an internal SOC review next Tuesday.

Best,
Alice Johnson
Director, IT Operations
Nimbus Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment prerequisites — network/KMS/audit items

Hi Alice — attaching a consolidated acceptance checklist and a sample network diagram. I highlighted the items that most commonly require clarification during SOC reviews. Quick notes up front:

1) Network - firewall and routing
   - Allow outbound TLS (443) to Redwood control plane endpoints for heartbeats and metrics (list in attachment).
   - Cross-AZ/VPC connectivity for model serving is optional — if you prefer isolation we can configure a single AZ pool.
   - Required ports: TCP 443 (control), TCP 1025-65535 (ephemeral for client comms), TCP 22 (admin, limited), UDP for internal telemetry if UDP used. See the attached spreadsheet for ports mapped by component.

2) KMS/HSM
   - We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Vault HSM integrations. For customer-managed KMS we need a service principal that can: Encrypt/Decrypt, GenerateDataKey, and DescribeKey. See sample IAM policy in the checklist.

3) Audit & Logging
   - Application logs (inference traces, errors) are delivered to the customer’s SIEM via syslog or secure HTTPS collector. Control-plane audit events (user actions, rollouts) can be archived to an S3 bucket or pushed to your Splunk instance. Retention is configurable; SOC teams typically ask for 365d.

4) Sizing guidance
   - For a 250 rps steady-state with median 1k-token responses, recommend 4x A100-80GB equivalent for model family X. Quantized 4-bit variants reduce memory and increase concurrency. We’ll share exact perf numbers after we validate your target sequences.

5) Blockers
   - Missing cross-account bucket permissions for KMS-wrapped artifacts, overly restrictive egress rules preventing control-plane callbacks, and lack of a service account for deployment automation are the most common blockers.

Next steps: can your IT team fill out the attached nimbus_network_requirements.xlsx and send back the completed network diagram? I’ll coordinate a 30‑minute handoff with Dev and Evelyn to walk through any gaps.

Attachments: redwood_private_onboard_checklist_v1.pdf, sample_network_diagram.png, nimbus_network_requirements.xlsx

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Thanks — quick responses inline:

1) Control-plane endpoints: 
   - control.redwood-api.com:443
   - metrics.redwood-api.com:443
   - upload.redwood-artifacts.com:443
   We can provide a published CIDR block for egress. If Nimbus wants a single static IP range for firewall allowlisting, we can provision NAT egress from our managed border gateway (this adds a small monthly charge and requires a cross-account peering for private deploy).

2) KMS: the sample IAM policy in the checklist is sufficient; for Vault we need the wrapped key material to be deliverable via our deployment agent. We should confirm the KMS key rotation window to ensure artifact decryptability during rollouts.

3) Logging: we can push control-plane audit events to an S3 bucket with server-side encryption (KMS) and lifecycle rules. For SIEM delivery we support: HTTPS collector with mTLS, syslog, and Splunk HTTP Event Collector. 365d retention is fine.

4) Sizing: I’ll run a quick perf estimate against their expected token mix and confirm whether 3x A100s is viable if they accept 5–10% higher p99 latency.

Laura — confirm the 10AM PT handoff and I’ll prepare a one‑page perf + egress options slide.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
